messages:
Jordan: Hi team — customer org-773 reporting streaming tokens/sec in Console flipping negative and TTFT showing -1200ms. Screenshot attached (img link). This is breaking billing and latency dashboards, can we triage?
Alex: Sorry to hear that — can you drop the time window and one example request id? Also which env (hosted/dedicated)?
Jordan: Hosted. Window: 2026-03-10 22:00 -> 23:00 UTC. Example request_id: req_0a3f5c. Repro steps: open Console -> Streaming -> select model xg-large -> window above. I can repro live.
Alex: Thanks. Pinging @mira_eng_metrics and @sam_runtime to check metrics rollup + ingestion. Any recent deploys? :eyes:
qa_bot: deploy-bot: metrics-ingest v2.4 deployed 2026-03-10T21:45 UTC to prod (canary 5%).
Mira: I see a small gap in the rollup window around ~22:13 UTC. Might be consumer offset drift between raw stream and rollup aggregator. Can you check Kafka consumer lag for group metrics-rollup for org-773?
Sam: We shipped a KV-cache change yesterday that touched sequence alignment during prefix merging — possible it produced negative deltas when replayed out-of-order. Will look at the rollup consumer logs.
Jordan: I pulled consumer metrics, here's CLI output I ran:```bash
kafka-consumer-groups --bootstrap-server kafka.prod:9092 --group metrics-rollup --describe --members
# output: PARTITION  OFFSET  LAG  CONSUMER-ID
0          105432  -12   consumer-12
1          203984  -3    consumer-12
```
Alex: Whoa negative LAG values — that suggests offsets moved backwards (maybe due to manual reset or a compacted topic rebase). Mira, can the rollup job emit a sanity check to avoid negative rate math?
Mira: We already have clamping logic but it assumes monotonic offsets. If offsets jump backwards (compaction+replay) the rollup delta calc can go negative. Quick mitigation: clamp negative deltas to 0 at presentation layer and kick a backfill for the affected window for accuracy.
Sam: I'll check runtime logs for the KV-cache replay artifacts. If replayed partial KV-cache entries arrive after rollup wrote aggregates, that could explain negative tokens/sec.
Alex: Temporary action items: 1) set UI to clamp negatives for streaming tokens/sec for the next 24h (reduce customer impact), 2) run/queue metrics-backfill for org-773 for 2026-03-10T22:00->23:00, 3) Sam/Mira investigate root cause and whether we need strict watermarking on the rollup consumer.
Sam: Also adding a watch to alert if consumer offsets move backwards more than 1 partition in a minute.
Mira: Backfill command I'm going to run (internal):```bash
metrics-backfill --tenant org-773 --start "2026-03-10T22:00:00Z" --end "2026-03-10T23:00:00Z" --job-name backfill-org-773-0310
```
Ops_oncall: FYI there was a short maintenance on kafka.prod at 21:50 UTC that coincides with the canary; connections were briefly bounced due to zookeeper leader transition. Might be related.
Alex: I'll update the customer: short-term clamp + we are running a backfill, expect corrected numbers within ~1 hour. Root-cause investigation ongoing.
Jordan: Thanks — customer notified. They asked for ETA on billing reconciliation since invoices use tokens/sec aggregates.
Alex: We'll add a billing reconciliation note and flag invoice for review if backfill changes totals. Will follow up in this thread once backfill finishes. :thumbsup:
Mira: Backfill started at 22:12 UTC, progress 0->100% in background, will post final status when done.
Jordan: Confirmed UI clamping reduced negative noise. Customer says charts look reasonable now.
Mira: Backfill complete, totals adjusted; no evidence of data loss, root cause: offset reset during leader transition + corner-case in KV-cache replay ordering. Patch to rollup will land today to add watermark-based monotonicity guard.
Alex: Closing loop — customer updated and billing team looped in. If you hit anything else ping here.
